statement.p: Find the area of one leaf of the "four-petaled rose" r =5 \sin 2\theta shown in the following figure:

static.solution:
r=5 \sin 2\theta in cartesian coordinates:
With r_0=5
We see that as \theta varies from 0 to \frac{\pi }{4} the radius r is increasing from 0 to 5, and when \theta varies from \frac{\pi }{4} to \frac{\pi}{2}, r is decreasing back to zero.
Hence, the leaf in the first quadrant is traced as \theta varies from 0 to \frac{\pi }{2}. The area of the leaf (the four leaves have equal areas) is thus A=\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi/2}{r}^{2} \,d\theta= \frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} 25\sin^{2} 2\theta \,d\theta. Using the identity \sin^{2} 2\theta =\frac{1- \cos 4\theta }{2} we get A = 12.5\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{ \cos 4\theta }{2}\right) \,d\theta= 12.5\left(\frac{\theta }{2}-\frac{ \sin 4\theta}{8}\right)\bigg|_{0}^{\pi/2}= 12.5\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{ \sin 2\pi }{8}\right)-0\right)= \frac{12.5\pi }{4} The area of one leaf is A=\frac{12.5\pi }{4}\approx 9.817.
